en.title: Dean Norris Has a Breaking Bad Fan-Made Mineral Collection
en.summary: Fans of the iconic AMC series Breaking Bad have found a unique way to honor actor Dean Norris. The star revealed he's amassed a significant collection of minerals gifted to him by attendees at conventions.
en.body:
## Hank Schrader's Unexpected Legacy

**Dean Norris**, forever etched in the minds of television aficionados as the DEA agent ASAC Hank Schrader from **Breaking Bad**, has found himself the recipient of a rather peculiar, yet fitting, fan-driven tribute. While Norris boasts a career spanning decades and numerous memorable roles, it's his tenure as Walter White's brother-in-law that continues to spark unique interactions with the show's passionate global fanbase. During a recent AMA session on Reddit, Norris shared an unexpected detail about his post-show life: a burgeoning collection of minerals, all gifted to him by fans at conventions. These aren't just any rocks; they are genuine minerals, a nod, no doubt, to the central, illicit commodity of the series itself.

> "I get handed minerals all the time at every convention and I save them all," Norris revealed. "It’s kind of a big collection now. I imagine I’ll continue to get them but I don’t go out and collect them myself."

This ongoing influx of geological gifts speaks volumes about the enduring connection fans feel to **Breaking Bad** and its characters. It's a testament to the show's narrative depth and the unforgettable performances that have cemented its place in television history. While Hank Schrader's journey was fraught with peril and ultimately tragedy, the way fans continue to engage with Norris and his character through these thoughtful, thematic gifts offers a lighter, more enduring legacy.

## The Fan Connection: More Than Just a Show

The phenomenon of fans gifting thematic items to actors is not new, but the specific nature of minerals for a show centered around methamphetamine production adds a layer of inside understanding that only dedicated viewers would grasp. It’s a subtle, yet powerful, acknowledgment of the intricate storytelling and the thematic elements that made **Breaking Bad** a critical and commercial success. For fans who have rewatched the series countless times, dissecting every plot twist and character arc, these gifts are a way to participate in the show's universe and show appreciation for the actors who brought these complex individuals to life. It’s this shared cultural language, built over five intense seasons, that fosters such unique and lasting fan engagement, turning convention meet-and-greets into something akin to a geological treasure hunt for **Dean Norris**.

## What's Next

While **Dean Norris** continues to build his impressive mineral collection, fans can revisit Hank Schrader's pivotal role in **Breaking Bad** on streaming platforms. Details regarding any future projects involving Norris that might further connect with his **Breaking Bad** legacy have not yet been announced.

content_raw: Although Dean Norris had a long career before  Breaking Bad , and a long career after it, it’s clear he knows what he’s most likely to be remembered for: ASAC Hank Schrader, a character who spent five seasons on the Vince Gilligan series making a long transition from a parody of the world’s most obnoxious brother-in-law into a complex, often tragic figure. And if he ever forgets  about ol’ Hank, Norris can apparently just look around his house and get many heavy, shiny reminders, because, holy crap, Breaking Bad  fans will simply not stop gifting this poor man minerals. This is per a recent AMA Norris did on Reddit , in which he addressed many questions about various aspects of his career—but most especially about  Breaking Bad . That includes some tidbits about the audition process—including remembering reflecting with co-star Betsy Brandt that their initial audition pages felt much more like a comedy than a drama—as well as thoughts on his time with late co-star RJ Mitte . (“He was so sweet, and innocent, just new to the business, and he just remained that sweet, innocent, kind kid, and I’m so sorry that he’s gone.”) But the AMA also contains quite a bit of conversation about minerals, which are not rocks, and which people will not stop gifting to Dean Norris at conventions. “I get handed minerals all the time at every convention and I save them all,” Norris revealed in one answer. “It’s kind of a big collection now,” he reveals in another. “I imagine I’ll continue to get them but I don’t go out and collect them myself.” Given how many people Norris has worked with over the years—he shares his impressions of  Total Recall -era Arnold Schwarzenegger (“really funny”) and  Hard To Kill -era Steven Seagal (“I thought he wasn’t that great of a karate guy”)—it’s understandable that Norris couldn’t get to every query tossed his way during the AMA. That being said, we did think it was kind of sad to see that the second-most-upvoted question in the mix somehow got missed by Norris and his team.
